newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM Litho beats forecasts, order book swells.
newsitem.headline: ASM Litho beats forecasts, order book swells.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography NV reported first-half earnings above market forecasts on Wednesday and said its order book was considerably fatter at the end of the period.
ASM Litho, in which Philips Electronics holds a 24 percent stake, said first-half net profit rose to 147 million guilders ($71.7 million) from 101 million in the same period of 1996.
After stripping out 31 million guilders of extraordinary income from the sale of a stake in a supplier, earnings were still above analysts' forecasts of 95 to 105 million guilders.
ASM Litho develops and sells photolithography projection systems, known as wafer steppers, that are vital to the production of semiconductors.
In the first half of 1997 the company shipped 95 machines, compared with 98 in the first half of 1996, but it said the decrease was more than offset by a higher average selling price.
The higher price reflected increased shipments of advanced 0.25 micron deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems, it added.
ASM Litho said it won orders for 136 wafer steppers during the first half of 1997, versus 101 in the first half of 1996.
This led to an order backlog of 135 units, worth 1.27 billion guilders, at the end of June, up from 94 units, worth 688 million guilders, at the end of December.
"ASML's market share is growing as ASML landed new customers during the first half of 1997. We are pleased with our prospects for the year," CEO Willem Maris said in a statement.
"After a slow start in 1997, business conditions have solidified and the company is building backlog," Maris said.
"In line with semiconductor market growth expectations, we are seeing in particular the ramp-up of deep UV photolithography," he added.
